searchText: Way to go y'all - awesome news This is weird. my node is requesting blobs from `16Uiu2HAkwy4MJBLsCvmuPwrfVX9GqNiGeppshnsbn2BgKskCtRDE`, the peer keeps returning 0 blobs instead of returning any error. Anyone else seeing this? I only see this for slots that did not process any blobs. which RPC is returning 0 blobs? this is `blobs_by_range` There aren't any blobs until slot 1637. Unless your request includes that then this is expected. In the same way nodes respond with 0 blocks for missed slots Currently prysm replies empty blobs, I'm guessing that's the wrong behavior then Yeah that's wrong behavior. tho the peer ID you posted was patched recently to not respond with empty blobs. Made a change while debugging issues syncing with lodestar. I haven't deployed the fix to the other nodes in the devnet tho Worth clarifying this in the spec that we should not be sending empty blobs? It's a little confusing because validators do gossip empty sidecar along side block Happy to open a draft PR Yup, please do. Thanks. Stiill something smells here, if we dont reply back empty blob, how could a node confidently validate that a chain has a data but it's just an empty data. Meaning `is_data_available` is not `false` for a slot with empty blob. I think there is a missing distinction here Ex: - Ask peer for blob at slot N - Peer replies nothing - how can I tell if the blob is missing or the blob is empty i suppose i can look at block's kzg commitments and decide i guess it depends on what you mean by empty blob. > - how can I tell if the blob is missing or the blob is empty isn't this the same thing? I see what you mean. You can tell whether there should be a blob or not for a given slot by checking the kzg commitments in the beacon block. Yep. I'll do that. Thanks for talking me through this np. this is probably worth clarifying in the spec as <@792822129019584562> asked a similar question earlier. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3174 🙏 i think it would be just sufficient if we change it to `"blobs_sidecar" **may be** skipped.` since someone sending a valid empty sidecar will not hurt

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: This is weird. my node is requesting blobs from `16Uiu2HAkwy4MJBLsCvmuPwrfVX9GqNiGeppshnsbn2BgKskCtRDE`, the peer keeps returning 0 blobs instead of returning any error. Anyone else seeing this?

excerpts.author: inphi
excerpts.content: I only see this for slots that did not process any blobs. which RPC is returning 0 blobs?

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: this is `blobs_by_range`

excerpts.author: inphi
excerpts.content: There aren't any blobs until slot 1637. Unless your request includes that then this is expected. In the same way nodes respond with 0 blocks for missed slots

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Currently prysm replies empty blobs, I'm guessing that's the wrong behavior then

excerpts.author: inphi
excerpts.content: Yeah that's wrong behavior.

excerpts.author: inphi
excerpts.content: tho the peer ID you posted was patched recently to not respond with empty blobs. Made a change while debugging issues syncing with lodestar. I haven't deployed the fix to the other nodes in the devnet tho

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
Worth clarifying this in the spec that we should not be sending empty blobs? 

It's a little confusing because validators do gossip empty sidecar along side block

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Happy to open a draft PR

excerpts.author: inphi
excerpts.content: Yup, please do. Thanks.

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Stiill something smells here, if we dont reply back empty blob, how could a node confidently validate that a chain has a data but it's just an empty data. Meaning `is_data_available` is not `false` for a slot with empty blob. I think there is a missing distinction here

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
Ex:
 - Ask peer for blob at slot N
 - Peer replies nothing
 - how can I tell if the blob is missing or the blob is empty

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: i suppose i can look at block's kzg commitments and decide

isn't this the same thing?

excerpts.author: inphi
